findings.title: retryCount delete branch is not scoped to SMS or scheduled:false
findings.body: The new OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` in the deleteMany has no `method` and no `scheduled` filter, so on every cron run it deletes any WorkflowReminder row whose retryCount exceeds 1 regardless of method (EMAIL/WHATSAPP too) or whether it was already successfully scheduled (`scheduled: true`, `referenceId` set). Today only this file increments retryCount, but the branch is clearly meant to target failed, unscheduled SMS reminders. If another reminder path ever increments retryCount, or a reminder reaches retryCount >= 2 and is then successfully scheduled, this deletes a reminder that still has a live Twilio message scheduled — leaving an orphaned SMS that will still be delivered. Scope the branch to `{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, scheduled: false, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`.

findings.title: retryCount increment uses a stale in-memory value, causing lost updates
findings.body: Both the else-branch and the catch-branch increment with `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, where `reminder.retryCount` was read once at the start of the batch by `findMany`. If two cron executions overlap (or the row is updated between read and write), both compute the same value from the same stale snapshot and the second write silently overwrites the first, so retryCount can fail to advance and the retry limit is never reached. Use an atomic increment (`{ increment: 1 }`) instead of read-then-write.

findings.title: Error handler performs a DB write that can itself throw and abort the whole batch
findings.body: The `catch (error)` block now performs `prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` before logging. If that update throws — e.g. the reminder was concurrently deleted by another cron run, or a transient DB error — the exception is thrown from inside the catch, escapes the loop, and the handler returns a 500 without processing the remaining reminders in the batch. Previously the catch only logged and continued. Wrap the increment so a failure there cannot abort the loop.

findings.title: Reminders skipped for empty message or missing sendTo never increment retryCount
findings.body: Both the success and failure branches live inside `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)`. When a reminder has no rendered message or no destination number, neither the success nor the else-branch executes, so retryCount is never incremented and the reminder is re-selected on every run indefinitely. That is exactly the infinite-rescheduling problem this PR is meant to fix, and it persists for these rows. Those rows should also bump retryCount (or be deleted) when they cannot be scheduled.

findings.title: No index supports the new retryCount filter in deleteMany
findings.body: The added `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` predicate in the global deleteMany has no index (the existing indexes are on bookingUid, workflowStepId, seatReferenceId, method/scheduled/scheduledDate, cancelled/scheduledDate). Because the OR includes this unindexed condition, the cron will scan the WorkflowReminder table on every invocation. Consider adding an index for the retry sweep or restructuring the predicate so it can use an existing index.

findings.title: No tests cover the new retry-count behavior
findings.body: The PR changes scheduling semantics (delete after N failures, increment on failure/error) but adds no tests for the new retryCount logic — neither for the delete threshold (`gt: 1`), nor for the increment on the falsy-schedule path, nor for the catch path. Add unit/integration coverage for the retry lifecycle, including deleting at the right count and not deleting successfully scheduled reminders.
